## Task
Research and compare the two candidate WebSearch query options for finding NixOS official documentation.

## Candidate Queries
1. "NixOS official manual"
2. "NixOS documentation"

## Acceptance Criteria
- Document what each query would likely return
- Identify which query is more precise and comprehensive
- Note any official NixOS documentation URLs discovered

## Deliverable
Add notes to this bead comparing the two options with a recommendation.
issue.notes:
## WebSearch Query Comparison for NixOS Documentation

### Query 1: "NixOS official manual"
**What it returns:**
- **Primary:** NixOS Manual (https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/)
- Learn Nix portal (https://nixos.org/learn/)
- NixOS Wiki (https://wiki.nixos.org/wiki/NixOS_Wiki)
- Nixpkgs Reference Manual (https://nixos.org/nixpkgs/manual/)
- Main NixOS website (https://nixos.org/)
- NixOS Installation Guide (https://nixos.wiki/wiki/NixOS_Installation_Guide)

**Characteristics:** Highly focused on the manual and official resources. The word "official" and "manual" make this query very specific.

### Query 2: "NixOS documentation"
**What it returns:**
- **Primary:** NixOS Manual (https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/)
- All resources from Query 1, plus:
- Nix reference manual (https://nix.dev/reference/nix-manual.html) - Additional official resource
- Community GitHub guide (https://github.com/mikeroyal/NixOS-Guide)
- Download page (https://nixos.org/download/)
- Official GitHub repos (https://github.com/nixos)

**Characteristics:** Broader scope while still maintaining precision. Captures both the manual and related documentation resources.

## Comparison Summary

| Aspect | Query 1 ("NixOS official manual") | Query 2 ("NixOS documentation") |
|--------|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Primary Result | NixOS Manual ✓ | NixOS Manual ✓ |
| Official Coverage | Excellent | Excellent+ |
| Community Resources | Minimal | Includes guides |
| Natural Language | Slightly formal | More natural |
| Breadth | Focused | Comprehensive |

## Recommendation

**Use "NixOS documentation"**

**Rationale:**
1. Both queries correctly identify the NixOS Manual as the primary resource
2. Query 2 provides slightly broader coverage including the Nix reference manual (nix.dev)
3. The query is shorter, more natural, and less redundant
4. "Documentation" is a more inclusive term that captures manuals, guides, wikis, and references

**Key Official URLs Discovered:**
- **Primary:** https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/ (NixOS Manual - the authoritative source)
- **Learning:** https://nixos.org/learn/ (Official learning portal)
- **Reference:** https://nixos.org/nixpkgs/manual/ (Nixpkgs manual)
- **Wiki:** https://wiki.nixos.org/wiki/NixOS_Wiki (Official community wiki)
- **Nix Reference:** https://nix.dev/reference/nix-manual.html (Nix package manager docs)

Both queries are effective and would serve the purpose well, but "NixOS documentation" has a slight edge in comprehensiveness and natural language usage.
issue.title: Research NixOS documentation search query options

issue.description:
## Evidence
plan.md Phase 5 feature 3 ('Time-aware context switching') specifies: 'Implementation: Entirely client-side using localStorage.' plan.md Section 12.3 (Data Privacy) states: 'No PII stored server-side. Favorites, commute journal, fare tracking, tap history — all localStorage, never sent to the backend.'

However packages/server/src/context-service.ts implements a full server-side context detection/persistence service (detectAndUpdateContextWithOwner, recordContextDetection, recordContextOverride, getContextTransitionsForOwner, etc.), backed by user_context and context_transitions SQLite tables created in packages/server/src/migration/migrations/016-add-trips-table.ts (lines ~60-90). This is exposed via live, mounted routes: app.use("/api/context/*", requireSameOrigin()) and app.get("/api/context", ...) in packages/server/src/app.ts (~line 2300).

Grepping the entire packages/web/src frontend for any call to /api/context returns zero matches as of this audit. The frontend's packages/web/src/stores/contextStore.ts implements context switching entirely client-side, exactly as the plan describes, and never calls this server API. The server-side context feature therefore appears to be dead code that was built in parallel with (not integrated into) the actual shipped client-side implementation, and that also stores tap/usage-pattern data server-side in contradiction of the plan's explicit no-PII-server-side promise.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Re-confirm (grep packages/web/src for /api/context, context-service, and any fetch/axios call referencing context) that no frontend code path calls this API before acting — if a caller is found, this bead's premise is wrong; document that and close without further action
- If confirmed unused, resolve the contradiction via ONE of:
  (a) Remove the unused server-side context feature: packages/server/src/context-service.ts, its /api/context* route mounts in app.ts, and the associated request schemas/imports, plus a plan for the now-unused user_context/context_transitions tables (a down-migration, or explicitly marking them deprecated-but-retained with a comment, whichever is lower-risk) — restoring alignment with plan.md's stated client-side design and privacy promise, OR
  (b) If there's a concrete near-term plan to wire the frontend to this API, add a 'Shipped Architecture Deviations' entry to plan.md Section 16 (alongside the existing auth-framework and map-screen entries) documenting why server-side context storage exists despite the stated client-side/no-PII design
- No change to the frontend's existing client-side contextStore.ts behavior is required under either path
issue.notes:
Verification complete: This issue was already resolved in August 2026. 

Confirmed:
- Frontend packages/web/src/ has ZERO calls to /api/context, context-service, or any fetch/axios context APIs (grep verified)
- Server-side packages/server/src/context-service.ts does NOT exist (deleted)
- Plan.md Section 16.6 already documents the resolution: 'Server-side context storage removed to align with client-side design'
- Database tables (user_context, context_transitions) exist only as DEPRECATED for backward compatibility per migration 016 comments

The premise of this bead was correct, but the work was already completed prior to this bead being claimed. Resolution path (a) was chosen: remove the unused server-side context feature, restoring alignment with plan.md's client-side/no-PII design.
issue.title: Resolve unused server-side /api/context feature (contradicts plan's client-side-only design and privacy promise)

issue.description:
## Goal
Build user trust through data transparency and provide critical fallback information when the system breaks down.

## Why This Matters
The worst moment for a commuter is when their line is suspended. The MTA says "use shuttle bus" but never says WHERE. And users need to know how fresh the data they're seeing actually is — especially given the A Division vs B Division accuracy gap.

## Key Decisions
- Shuttle bus stops are a curated static JSON lookup (not dynamic — MTA doesn't provide this data electronically)
- Start with 10 most common suspension segments, grow incrementally
- Data freshness shows per-feed age with color coding: green <15s, amber 45-90s, red >90s
- Per-arrival feedName field lets frontend show which feed each arrival came from

## Acceptance Criteria
- Shuttle bus info displayed for 10+ common suspension segments
- Data freshness visible on all station detail views with color-coded staleness

## Dependencies
- Requires Phase 3 (alert parsing for NO_SERVICE detection)
- Requires Phase 1 (feed pipeline with per-feed timestamps)

## Goal
Transform the app from a data display into a predictive, context-aware commute companion that learns and anticipates.

This is where the app becomes genuinely differentiated. No competitor predicts delays before the MTA announces them, no competitor tracks your trip and shares ETA, no competitor learns your patterns to auto-sort favorites, and no competitor builds a personal commute history.

- Offline countdown working underground with cached data

## Child of: mtamyway-d624b0f7

## Objective
Verify that CSRF protection is working correctly on state-changing API operations.

## Scope
- Test CSRF token generation for authenticated sessions
- Verify CSRF token validation on POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH requests
- Test that CSRF protection is active on /api/* routes
- Verify state-changing requests without CSRF tokens are rejected
- Test that GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests don't require CSRF tokens
- Verify CSRF token expiry and refresh behavior

## Acceptance Criteria
- CSRF tokens are generated and included in responses
- State-changing requests with valid CSRF tokens are accepted

issue.notes:
Created comprehensive integration tests for CSRF protection on state-changing API operations.

## Tests Created
- File: packages/server/src/integration/csrf-state-changing-operations.test.ts
- 53 test cases covering all acceptance criteria

## Security Vulnerability Discovered
Found a real security bug in production CSRF configuration:

**Issue**: Path '//api/trip' (singular) in excludePaths accidentally excludes '/api/trips' (plural) routes due to startsWith() matching logic in CSRF middleware (line 262 of csrf-protection.ts).

**Impact**: Routes like POST /api/trips, PATCH /api/trips/:tripId/notes, DELETE /api/trips/:tripId are NOT protected by CSRF tokens.

**Fix Required**: Change '//api/trip' to '/api/trip/' (with trailing slash) or use exact matching instead of startsWith() in CSRF middleware.

## Test Coverage
✅ CSRF token generation for authenticated sessions
✅ CSRF token validation on POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH requests  
✅ CSRF protection active on /api/* routes
✅ State-changing requests without CSRF tokens rejected
✅ GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests bypass CSRF validation
✅ CSRF token expiry and refresh behavior
✅ Existing API behavior preserved for public endpoints
✅ CSRF error responses are clear and secure

## Test Results
- 40 tests PASSED - CSRF protection working correctly for most routes
- 13 tests FAILED - Revealed the security vulnerability above

The integration tests successfully validated CSRF protection and discovered a production security configuration issue that needs immediate fixing.

issue.description:
Found 2026-09-05 while writing OnboardingFlow unit tests (mtamyway-65ebaacf). Reproduced and measured; tests for the nearby step are blocked on this fix, so the Phase 1 onboarding coverage gap stays open until it lands.

MECHANISM — packages/web/src/components/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx:
:nearbyStations is recomputed inline on every render (lines ~78-81, 'findNearbyStations(...)' returns a fresh array), and the pre-select effect (lines ~98-108) lists it as a dependency:
  useEffect(() => { if (step === 'nearby' && nearbyStations.length > 0) setSelectedStations(nearbyStations.map(...)); }, [step, nearbyStations]);
While step === 'nearby', every pass sees a new nearbyStations identity, calls setSelectedStations with a new array, and forces another render. Unbounded.

TRIGGER: any first-run user who grants location inside the NYC area with >=1 station within 2 km — i.e. the primary onboarding path. The tab freezes; nothing catches it because OnboardingFlow had no unit test (the Phase 1 verdict gap this bead's sibling filed).

EVIDENCE (jsdom + @testing-library/react, vitest): rendering the flow, granting location and advancing to the nearby step drives findNearbyStations past 875 calls in ~250 ms with heap climbing monotonically (71 MB -> 127 MB over 150 calls before a budget throw, loop continuing past the throw), while a parent wrapper re-renders only twice — the loop is OnboardingFlow re-rendering itself. Capping the worker at 4 GB ends in 'JavaScript heap out of memory'. Same signature with 1 nearby station or 3, and unrelated to the mocks used (real nearbyStations math, real favorites store).

FIX OPTIONS: memoize the nearby list (useMemo on coordinates/stations/complexes/loading) so the effect deps settle, or key the pre-select effect on nearbyStations.length like the auto-advance effect above it, or move the pre-select into the continue handler / a ref-guard. Whichever is chosen, the selected-stations state must still survive the toggle interaction.

AFTER THE FIX: extend packages/web/src/components/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.test.tsx (created by mtamyway-65ebaacf, which deliberately omits nearby-step coverage and documents why in its header) with: auto-advance from location to nearby, pre-selection of all nearby stations, 2 km filtering, toggle-off before continue, favorites created on continue, and skip-from-nearby. Note the sibling bead mtamyway-7ed5c96b (rules-of-hooks early return in HomeScreen.tsx) is a separate crash in a different file and does not cover this.
issue.title: Fix infinite render loop in OnboardingFlow nearby step (pre-select effect deps on a new array every render)

Research and document the standard path where ripgrep (rg) is installed on NixOS systems.

## Acceptance Criteria

issue.notes:
## Research Findings: NixOS ripgrep Binary Path

### Standard NixOS Path
The standard path where ripgrep (rg) is installed on NixOS systems is:

**/run/current-system/sw/bin/rg**

### Verification
- `which rg` → /run/current-system/sw/bin/rg
- `command -v rg` → /run/current-system/sw/bin/rg
- Confirmed on NixOS 26.05

### Path Structure
`/run/current-system/sw/bin/rg` is a symlink to the actual binary in the Nix store:
- Symlink: /run/current-system/sw/bin/rg
- Target: /nix/store/<hash>-ripgrep-15.1.0/bin/rg

### Other NixOS Binary Locations (Not Applicable for ripgrep)
- ~/.nix-profile/bin/ - User-specific packages (not present)
- /etc/profiles/per-user/<user>/bin/ - User profile binaries (not present)

### Recommendation
Use `/run/current-system/sw/bin/rg` as the standard NixOS ripgrep path. This path:
- Is stable across NixOS installations
- Is automatically updated when the system configuration changes
- Follows the NixOS convention of symlinking /run/current-system/sw/ to the active system generation
issue.title: Determine NixOS ripgrep binary path

issue.notes:
Investigation complete. Root cause + full evidence in docs/notes/needle-fallback-gate-quarantine-cluster.md (commit daf24687, pushed 84ab6154..daf24687).

ROOT CAUSE: NEEDLE's fallback verification gate is unwinnable in this workspace by construction. Since 4401ba25 (08-29) removed the verification block the workspace is gate-less; the fallback gate shipped in needle 0.6.2 (54241f8e 09-15 + 4657aa60 09-16) then selects `npm test` and runs it inside a bare `git archive HEAD` extraction that has no node_modules and no install step. mta-my-way's test script is `vitest run`, so verification deterministically fails `sh: line 1: vitest: command not found` exit 127 regardless of bead content. Failure-count reaches the quarantine threshold (default 5, config/mod.rs default_quarantine_after_failures); while the workspace is gate-degraded (N-T22 fingerprint path + the 09-19 ~/scratch ENOSPC execution-error path, both live in gate-health/96c977accde8.json: degraded:true, consecutive_errors:3), every penalty also stamps `degraded-window-failure:<pre-count>` (37 markers, 13 beads, first 09-17T21:07:57Z, last 09-22T06:30:54Z, peaking 09-21 with 29 markers/9 beads). Restoration — the only mechanism that undoes those markers — requires a clean gate run (restore_degraded_workspace is called only after "all validation gates passed", outcome/mod.rs ~2470), which an unwinnable gate can never produce: a deadlock, not a leak. Result: 9 unrelated open beads cycling at quarantine-round:3 with failure-count 5-6 and identical label progression. None of the cohort is individually broken.

KEY EVIDENCE (all re-verified live at close time; commands: python3 sqlite3 on .beads/beads.db ?mode=ro over attempt_outcomes/labels/events; live repro in mktemp -d): (1) version boundary exact — verified_success outcomes store-wide are 0.6.0/0.6.1 only (58), gate:fallback_node are 0.6.2-0.6.7 only (371); first failure a982bc46 09-17T17:50:22Z on 0.6.2. (2) Daily histogram reproduced (09-18: 64/66; 09-23: 57/57). (3) Live repro: git archive HEAD | tar -x -> no node_modules, npm test -> exit 127, byte-identical to the stored degraded_summary. (4) This investigation's own dispatch failed the same gate (fingerprint window entry ae915f0c 15:09:09Z, same fingerprint 51702ee4c8fb). (5) Every round:1/2/3 event timestamp in the doc reproduced from the events table, incl. the 09-17 17:11:52-:59Z six-bead sweep antedating the first fallback failure by ~39 min (pre-window decline regime). (6) All five named commits in E3 (dcfe438a, c732f675, af1494cd, ebbfe383, 3ba5bfdc) appear in fallback-failure evidence refs — real landed work penalized by the verifier. (7) Source-level: NODE_COMMAND="npm test" (validation/fallback.rs), zero npm ci/install/node_modules in the extraction path, DEGRADATION_THRESHOLD=3 (gate_health.rs), quarantine threshold 5.

VERIFICATION RUN: npm run lint -> 4 errors, all pre-existing and untouched by this change (gitignored vapid-keys.json local-only baseline + three files from other workers' untracked WIP); the deliverable file is markdown-only, 0 lint findings. npm test not run as a pass/fail gate: change is docs-only and the working tree holds other workers' WIP (standing known-red baseline owned by ee10b029+d2c54c27); the CI-gate defect documented here is itself the reason the pipeline is red — fixing it is mtamyway-4b6d02a2's scope.

MILDer four (07689b17, a982bc46, 8fd8f402, 3944486f): same mechanism, same fingerprint, but none progressed to round:3 (counts stayed under threshold; dispatch into the workspace stopped after 09-22 — 09-22/09-23 failures are exclusively the 9ad0760f epoch loop, 3944486f x3, and this attempt). They need the gate fix (G1), nothing more; no dependency changes made.

976cd42f ("Fix CI failures and iterate until pipeline is green") is unbounded AND unsatisfiable from inside this workspace — its dispatch gate is the broken thing. Recommendation recorded in the doc: rescope it to the gate repair or close it on the G1 fix bead.

Fix directions G1-G5 for mtamyway-4b6d02a2 in the doc; recovery shape: fix the gate first — the first clean verification then clears the state file and undo_degraded_window_penalties automatically returns all 13 marked beads to pre-window counts and drops their quarantine labels (no manual bead surgery).

## What
Build the transfer analysis engine that computes multi-leg routes from real-time arrival data for a given origin/destination pair.

## Subtasks
- [ ] Station graph (graph.ts): build weighted graph from transfers.json + complexes.json
- [ ] Travel times (travel-times.ts): load scheduled inter-station times, index by route+direction
- [ ] Engine (engine.ts): for origin→destination, find all direct routes and transfer routes
- [ ] Direct route scoring: line + next arrival at origin + travel time to destination
- [ ] Transfer route scoring: first leg + walking time + wait at transfer + second leg travel time

- [ ] Rank all routes by total estimated arrival time at destination

- Walking time defaults to transfers.txt min_transfer_time, fallback 180s

The captured line is the console.warn in pushLocalTrips' permanent-rejection path (packages/web/src/hooks/useJournalSync.ts:281) — deliberate behavior: a 4xx trip upload is quarantined in syncState.rejected so a bad payload is never retried, the local record is kept, and the refusal is logged. issue.description:
The live deployment.yaml pins the container to ronaldraygun/mta-my-way
with tag "latest" and imagePullPolicy Always (in the declarative-config
repo, path: k8s / apexalgo-iad / mta-my-way / deployment.yaml). This
violates the workspace CI policy ("Never use latest image tags --
always pin to a specific digest or version tag") and means ArgoCD and
kubectl cannot diff or roll back to a known-good image -- every push to
main silently rolls forward with no pinned prior state to revert to if
a build regresses.

Fix: have the mta-my-way image build template (declarative-config repo,
under k8s / iad-ci / argo-workflows) tag images with the git SHA (or the
semver from VERSION) in addition to "latest", and update deployment.yaml
in declarative-config to reference that pinned tag/digest instead of
"latest". Bump the pinned tag as part of the normal deploy flow
(commit, push, ArgoCD sync), same as any other manifest change.

Referenced in this repo's docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (2026-07-20) as
follow-up work.

Why this is its own child: every prior green reading on this repo came from a tree carrying uncommitted WIP, so local green never reached CI - the parent's 486 errors were invisible locally for exactly that reason. The chain's original terminal verify child mtamyway-c6439d68 was closed while its three upstream blockers were still open, which left the parent ungated and got it re-dispatched to failure-count:5.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every fix from the chain is committed and pushed to origin main with explicit paths. Uncommitted fixes are invisible to CI; that is the failure mode this child exists to rule out.
- Measured on a tree with no uncommitted changes under packages/ - a fresh clone of pushed origin/main, or the shared checkout once git status --porcelain is clean for the touched paths. Do not measure on working-tree state.
- npm run typecheck (or npx tsc --build --force) exits 0 with zero errors in packages/web and packages/shared.
- No new error class appeared: a file outside the 8-file list above now erroring is a regression from a chain step, not a pass.
- Evidence recorded in docs/ci-reports/ alongside the 2026-09-04 typecheck-gate monitor write-up.

Re-measure on pickup - concurrent workers land to this tree continuously, so the count may differ from the 37 above. Done when: typecheck exits 0 on a clean checkout of pushed origin/main, with the evidence committed and handed to the CI-verification child.

issue.notes:
## Middleware File Structure Analysis

### Location
- Main index: `packages/server/src/middleware/index.ts`
- Directory contains 51 TypeScript files (excluding tests)
- 46 export block statements in index file

### Export Pattern
**Named exports grouped by module:**
- Each export block imports from a specific module file (e.g., `from "./authentication.js"`)
- Related functions/types grouped together in single export blocks
- Types explicitly marked with `type` keyword when exported
- Consistent pattern: `export { name1, name2, type TypeName } from "./module.js"`

### Module Organization (by export order)

**Basic HTTP Layer:**
- request-id, rate-limiter, cors, request-limits

**Validation & Input Security:**
- security-headers (CSP functions)
- validation (body, query, params)
- content-type, header-validation
- input-sanitization, path-traversal
- parameter-pollution (HPP protection)

**Caching Strategies:**
- cache module exports 9 cache types (static, api, health, etag, conditional-get, immutable, etc.)

**Authentication & Session Management:**
- authentication (28 exports: API keys, sessions, passwords, rate limiting, types)
- password-management (internal utilities)
- csrf-protection (10 exports)
- token-encryption (17 exports: encryption/decryption, key management)
- cookie-security (20 exports: signing, validation, session cookies)
- session-security (18 exports: risk assessment, device trust, impossible travel)
- concurrent-session-management (18 exports: session cleanup, conflict resolution)

**Authorization:**
- authorization (14 exports: resource access, RBAC integration, audit logging)
- rbac (30 exports: permissions, roles, hierarchical checks, type exports)
- enhanced-authorization (11 exports: resource types, batch auth, ownership)
- authorization-security (8 exports: time/location-based, behavioral analysis)
- dynamic-rbac-cache (23 exports: permission checks, cache invalidation, overrides)

**JWT & Token Security:**
- jwt-validation (11 exports: validation, verification, replay detection)
- enhanced-jwt-security (15 exports: compromise detection, device fingerprinting, revocation)

**HTTP Security Protections:**
- ssrf-protection (URL validation, safe fetch, MTA feed allowlist)
- host-header-protection
- dependency-security (security checks, reports)
- subresource-integrity (SRI hash generation/validation)
- http-response-splitting (CRLF injection protection)
- http-request-smuggling (content-length validation, chunked encoding checks)
- http-method-restrictions (safe/dangerous method classification)

**Additional Protections:**
- mass-assignment (field filtering, sanitized body generation)
- open-redirect (URL validation, safe redirect creation)
- json-depth-protection
- response-size-limits (streaming, pagination, size estimation)

**Security Monitoring & Logging:**
- security-logging
- audit-log (25 exports: event logging, querying, export, retention)
- structured-audit-log (19 exports: structured events, compliance reporting, incident detection)
- suspicious-activity-notifications (10 exports)

**Rate Limiting & CAPTCHA:**
- auth-rate-limit (IP banning, tiered limits, cleanup)
- captcha (verification, challenge generation, attempt tracking)

**Admin & Key Management:**
- admin-operations (admin checks, bulk operations, audit export)
- api-key-management (key CRUD, ownership checks, validation)
- enhanced-authentication (security incidents, auth data invalidation)

### Key Observations

1. **Comprehensive Security Coverage**: 51 modules covering all OWASP Top 10 categories plus advanced features
2. **Type-Safe API**: Every module exports TypeScript types alongside functions
3. **Consistent Naming**: `validateX`, `requireX`, `checkX`, `getSafeX` patterns throughout
4. **Layered Security**: Multiple overlapping protections (e.g., CSRF in both csrf-protection and cookie-security)
5. **Integration Points**: RBAC integrates with authorization, authentication integrates with sessions
6. **Export Pattern**: Named exports from barrel index, no default exports observed

### Next Step
The export pattern analysis provides the foundation for the next bead: 'Analyze middleware export pattern' — this will examine how individual modules structure their exports (named vs default, re-exports, internal utilities, etc.).
issue.title: Document middleware file structure

## Task
Research the fundamental concepts of NixOS system profiles and activation scripts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Understand what NixOS system profiles are
- Document how /run/current-system/ is created during system activation

This is child bead 1 of 4 for documenting /run/current-system/sw/bin/ purpose.
issue.notes:
## Research Findings: NixOS System Profiles and Activation Scripts

### What are NixOS System Profiles?

**System Profile Location:** `/nix/var/nix/profiles/system`

The system profile is a Nix profile that contains all system generations. Each generation represents a complete, immutable system configuration stored in the Nix store.

- Managed via `nix-env -p /nix/var/nix/profiles/system`
- Each generation is a store path containing the complete system configuration
- Systemd-boot iterates through all generations to configure boot entries
- Can roll back to previous generations via `nixos-rebuild switch --rollback` or GRUB

**System Profile Structure (this system):**
- Current profile: `/nix/var/nix/profiles/system -> system-17-link`
- Latest generation: `system-17-link -> /nix/store/57dd4gicqyhvfpqj3mmibgxpi89isgl4-nixos-system-codinghome-26.05.20260826.062346a`
- Previous generations: system-1-link through system-16-link

### How /run/current-system is Created

**Creation Mechanism:** Atomic symlink replacement during activation

From activation-script.nix (line 157):
```bash
ln -sfn "$(readlink -f "$systemConfig")" /run/current-system
```

**Purpose:**
- Represents the currently active system configuration
- Points to a store path in `/nix/store/` (the activated generation)
- Serves as a garbage collection root
- Provides access to system-wide packages via `/run/current-system/sw/bin/`

**Actual path on this system:**
```bash
/run/current-system -> /nix/store/57dd4gicqyhvfpqj3mmibgxpi89isgl4-nixos-system-codinghome-26.05.20260826.062346a
```

**Structure of /run/current-system:**
- `/activate` - Main activation script (5516 bytes, bash)
- `/dry-activate` - Test activation without making changes
- `/bin/` - Contains switch-to-configuration script
- `/sw` - **symlink to system packages** (`/nix/store/17n18lm73c7z2c076anllnknlfx4wqmy-system-path`) 
  - This is where `/run/current-system/sw/bin/` comes from
  - Contains: bin/, sbin/, lib/, share/, etc.
- `/init` - the init system (systemd or bootStage2)
- `/prepare-root` - root filesystem preparation (systemd-initrd)
- `/etc` - symlink to `/etc` configuration
- `/systemd` - systemd package
- `/kernel` - kernel bzImage
- `/initrd` - initramfs
- `/kernel-modules` - kernel modules
- `/firmware` - kernel firmware
- `/boot.json` - bootloader configuration
- `/nixos-version` - NixOS label (26.05.20260826.062346a)
- `/kernel-params` - kernel parameters (root=fstab loglevel=4 lsm=landlock,yama,bpf)

### Key Activation Scripts and Files

**1. /run/current-system/activate**
Main activation script that:
- Sets up /bin/sh symlink (snippet: binsh)
- Creates user accounts and groups (snippet: users)
- Mounts special filesystems (snippet: specialfs)
- Sets up /etc configuration (snippet: etc)
- Validates password hash algorithms (snippet: hashes)
- Configures kernel module loading (snippet: modprobe)
- Installs secrets via sops (snippet: setupSecrets)
- Configures udev and firmware paths (snippet: udevd)
- Creates /usr/bin/env symlink (snippet: usrbinenv)
- **Creates /run/current-system symlink** (line 157)

**2. /run/current-system/bin/switch-to-configuration**
Wrapper script that:
- Sets environment variables (OUT, TOPLEVEL, DISTRO_ID, etc.)
- Executes the wrapped switch-to-configuration binary
- Used by nixos-rebuild to activate new configurations

**3. system.build.toplevel (top-level.nix)**
- Path: `nixos/modules/system/activation/top-level.nix`
- Creates the system derivation via `pkgs.stdenvNoCC.mkDerivation`
- Generates a store path named: `nixos-system-${config.system.name}-${config.system.nixos.label}`
- Contains symlinks to kernel, systemd units, init scripts
- Includes the `switch-to-configuration` script

**4. activation-script.nix**
- Path: `nixos/modules/system/activation/activation-script.nix`
- Generates the main activation script
- Handles both normal and dry-activation modes
- Processes activation snippets in dependency order
- Creates `/run/current-system` atomically

### The Activation Process

Complete flow for `nixos-rebuild switch`:

1. **Build:** `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.mymachine.config.system.build.toplevel`
   - Evaluates configuration.nix
   - Builds the system derivation
   - Produces a store path (result)

2. **Set Profile:** `nix-env -p /nix/var/nix/profiles/system --set ./result`
   - Creates a new generation in the system profile
   - Makes the new generation the current profile

3. **Activate:** `./result/bin/switch-to-configuration switch`
   - Runs activation scripts
   - Creates `/run/current-system` symlink
   - Updates `/etc` configuration files
   - Restarts systemd services
   - Sets configuration as default boot target

### Key Configuration Files

- **`/etc/nixos/configuration.nix`** or **`/etc/nixos/flake.nix`** - System configuration
- **`nixos/modules/system/activation/top-level.nix`** - Builds system.toplevel
- **`nixos/modules/system/activation/activation-script.nix`** - Generates activation script
- **`nixos/modules/system/activation/activatable-system.nix`** - Activatable system logic

### Modern Developments

**Deprecation of Activation Scripts:**
- GitHub Issue #475305 tracks deprecation
- New `nixos-init` allows interpreter-less boot
- Encouraged to use systemd services instead of `userActivationScripts`
- Some NixOS systems already build without activation scripts

**Sources:**
- [NixOS Discourse - System profiles](https://discourse.nixos.org/t/system-profiles-and-switch-to-configuration/52315)
- [NixOS activation-script.nix source](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/system/activation/activation-script.nix)
- [NixOS top-level.nix source](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/system/activation/top-level.nix)
- [Beginner's guide to /run/current-system](https://xn--w5d.cc/2020/08/31/current-system-nixos.html)
- [NixOS Wiki - Replacing activationScripts](https://wiki.nixos.org/wiki/Replacing_activationScripts)

**System-Specific Details (codinghome, 2026-08-28):**
- Current system: NixOS 26.05.20260826.062346a
- System profile: 17 generations
- System path: /nix/store/17n18lm73c7z2c076anllnknlfx4wqmy-system-path
- Kernel: Linux 6.18.46
- Systemd: 260.2
- Activation script size: 5516 bytes
- Uses sops for secret management

## Scanner Finding

**Scanner:** test
**Severity:** 2/5 (1=critical)
**File:** (unknown)

**Description:**
[22m[39mFailed to fetch CSRF token: [TypeError: Failed to parse URL from /api/csrf-token] {

---
This issue was detected by the pulse strand during a codebase health scan.
issue.notes:
Audited and dispositioned: transient test-output noise, no product defect, not reproducible on the current tree.

Emitter (sole source repo-wide): packages/web/src/lib/api.ts:86 — the catch in fetchCsrfToken() logging console.error("Failed to fetch CSRF token:", error).

Mechanism: Node's undici fetch rejects relative URLs. In the web vitest project (jsdom) the global fetch is still undici, so any test that reaches a state-changing fetchJson() (POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH in api.ts) with no csrf_token cookie and global fetch left unstubbed throws exactly "TypeError: Failed to parse URL from /api/csrf-token", which api.ts catches and logs. Proven in one line: `node -e 'fetch("/api/csrf-token")...'` -> "threw: TypeError: Failed to parse URL from /api/csrf-token". In a real browser the same call resolves against the page origin, so the production code path is correct; journalApi.ts's equivalent deliberately swallows silently, which is why only api.ts can emit this string.

Trigger surface today is fully covered: the only POST-path api methods (analyzeCommute, subscribePush, unsubscribePush, updatePushSubscription) are exercised by useCommute.test.ts / useCommute.states.test.ts (vi.mock of ../lib/api, real api.ts never runs) and usePushNotifications.test.ts / api.test.ts / apiEnhanced.test.ts (global fetch stubbed). No current test reaches real fetch on a POST path.

Reproduction: ran the scanner's exact command (`npm test` at repo root — all four vitest projects, 7095 tests, ~297s) at the predispatch SHA bc4c7578 (== current HEAD, nothing has landed since the 08:39Z scan) plus the current WIP — zero occurrences of the message; the web project alone also zero. The scan captured a single occurrence (failure-count:1) from an intermediate state of the shared checkout's uncommitted WIP at scan time; that WIP has since moved (91 dirty files, e.g. the useTripTracker/TransferDetail worker's edits).

Unrelated red seen during the run, not attributable to this finding: 7 web failures from another worker's uncommitted useTripTracker.test.ts/useTripTracker.ts WIP, plus 2 FareTracker.test.tsx failures, and the known-red server auth/security suites — all left untouched.

No file changes made: nothing to fix in product code (the console.error is correct in-browser diagnostics and silencing it would hide real failures), and no test currently produces the noise.

issue.description:
## What
Detect delays before MTA announces them by tracking VehiclePosition changes across consecutive polls. When trains are stopped or moving abnormally slowly, fire a synthetic early-warning alert.

## Subtasks
- [ ] delay-detector.ts: track each tripId position across consecutive 30s polls
- [ ] Compute actual inter-station traversal time vs scheduled baseline from travel-times.json
- [ ] Single-train alert: when actual > 1.5x scheduled for a segment, flag that segment
- [ ] Line-level alert: when 2+ trains on same line show slowdowns, escalate to line alert
- [ ] Synthetic alert generation: create StationAlert with source: "predicted", distinct severity
- [ ] Expose via GET /api/alerts with source field so frontend can display distinctly (amber dotted border)
- [ ] Tuning: configurable threshold multiplier (default 1.5x) and minimum sample count (2 trains)

## Considerations
- A Division (ATS) will produce much better predictions than B Division (Bluetooth beacons)
- False positives are worse than false negatives — start conservative (2.0x threshold) and tune down
- Terminal stations will show trains "stopped" for extended periods — exclude first/last stops
issue.title: Predictive delay detection from VehiclePosition diffs

issue.description:
## Task
Research and document the purpose and function of /run/current-system/sw/bin/ on NixOS.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Explain what /run/current-system/sw/bin/ is
- Document how it is created/populated
- Explain its relationship to the NixOS system profile
- Record findings in the parent bead's notes

## Context
This is child bead 1 of 3 for researching NixOS system binary directory structure.
issue.notes:
Research completed and documented.

## Key Findings

### What is /run/current-system/sw/bin?
- Runtime symlink to the current system generation's binaries
- Points to /nix/store/[hash]-system-path/bin/
- Every binary is a symlink to actual binaries in /nix/store/
- Volatile - created during nixos-rebuild, lost on reboot

### How it is created/populated
1. nixos-rebuild evaluates configuration.nix and NixOS modules
2. Collects all packages from environment.systemPackages
3. Builds a special 'system-path' store path that consolidates all packages
4. Updates /nix/var/nix/profiles/system (persistent profile)
5. Creates /run/current-system symlinks (volatile runtime path)

### Relationship to NixOS system profile
- /run/current-system = volatile, currently running system
- /nix/var/nix/profiles/system = persistent, all generations
- Both point to same Nix store generation when running
- System profile provides boot menu entries

### Documentation
Full findings documented in:
docs/research/nixos-binary-directory-structure.md

Verified on live NixOS 26.05.20260826.062346a system.
issue.title: Document /run/current-system/sw/bin purpose

issue.description:
## Evidence
docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (2026-07-20, "Decouple the Core Read Path from Persistent-Volume-Backed State") names an "incremental first step, deployable before the full manifest split": make the better-sqlite3 opens in packages/server/src/push/subscriptions.ts lazy/best-effort rather than a startup-blocking call in index.ts, "so an unwritable or corrupt /data doesn't crash process startup even in cases where the mount technically succeeds but the filesystem underneath is bad."

This has NOT been done. In packages/server/src/index.ts (~line 149-150):

  const pushDbPath = process.env["PUSH_DB_PATH"] ?? join(DATA_DIR, "subscriptions.db");
  initPushDatabase(pushDbPath);
  const pushDb = getPushDatabase();

initPushDatabase() (packages/server/src/push/subscriptions.ts) calls `new Database(dbPath)` directly with no try/catch. This whole block runs before the HTTP server starts listening, so any exception here still crashes the entire process before /api/health, /api/arrivals, /api/stations etc. can ever come up — i.e. the exact single-point-of-failure ADR-001 is meant to eliminate is still fully present in code, even though the plan document already claims this was addressed.

Correction to ADR-001's own description while investigating this: the ADR and notes/bf-2uz2z.md both refer to a second SQLite file "alert_history.db" / env var ALERT_HISTORY_PATH for alert history, backed by its own db open. Repo-wide search (git log --all and grep across packages/server/src) turns up zero references to ALERT_HISTORY_PATH or an alert-history db file anywhere in actual code — only in the plan/notes prose. README's Project Structure section confirms there is only one SQLite file in packages/server/data (subscriptions, trips, sessions all in the same db opened via initPushDatabase/getPushDatabase). Scope this bead to that single db; if a genuinely separate alert-history store is later intended, note that as a documentation follow-up rather than assuming it already exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Wrap the initPushDatabase() call path (or the module-level open in subscriptions.ts) so a failure to open/init the db (corrupt file, EIO, read-only fs) is caught and logged, not thrown to the top of index.ts's startup sequence
- On failure, the process continues starting: HTTP server binds and listens, and stateless/read-only endpoints (/api/health, /api/arrivals/*, /api/stations, /api/routes, /api/alerts, /api/commute/analyze, static PWA assets) keep working
- Endpoints that require the db (push subscribe, trip tracking, sessions, password-reset, security persistence) degrade gracefully — return a clear 503/"degraded" rather than crashing the process — when the db failed to open
- /api/health reports the push/db subsystem as degraded (not overall service failure) when this happens
- Add or update a test that simulates an unopenable db path and asserts the server still starts and /api/health responds
- Correct the "alert_history.db" / ALERT_HISTORY_PATH references in docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 and notes/bf-2uz2z.md to reflect that there is one db file, not two (small doc fix, can be folded into this bead or split into a docs-only follow-up comment)

Running `vitest` spawns 20 workers, each consuming ~50-65% CPU. When multiple instances run (or a dev leaves tests running), this cripples the entire Hetzner box with load averages of 40+.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Only one vitest instance can run at a time on this machine
- Options:
  1. **Lockfile mechanism**: vitest checks for a lockfile before starting; second instance waits or exits with a message
  2. **vitest.config.ts poolOptions**: limit `maxWorkers` and/or use `--single-thread` / `--max-workers` flag
  3. **Process guard**: wrapper script that kills stale vitest processes before starting a new run
- Fallback: move heavy test suites to CI (iad-ci Argo Workflows) and keep local runs lightweight (`vitest --run` not watch mode by default)

## Notes

- Current vitest config likely uses default pool size which scales to CPU count
- Consider adding `vitest.config.ts` pool options: `pool: 'forks', poolOptions: { forks: { maxForks: 4 } }`
- Watch mode (`vitest` without `--run`) is the main culprit — it keeps workers alive indefinitely
issue.title: Enforce single vitest instance — prevent parallel test runs from hogging CPU

issue.description:
## What
Build the script that downloads MTA GTFS static data (stops.txt, routes.txt, transfers.txt, stop_times.txt) and processes it into optimized JSON files: stations.json, routes.json, transfers.json, travel-times.json, complexes.json.

## Why
This is the foundation for ALL station-level features. Station search, favorites display, transfer engine, walking comparison, complex mapping — everything needs this processed data. It runs at build time (baked into the container image) and periodically when MTA updates schedules.

## Subtasks
- [ ] Download script: fetch gtfs_subway.zip and gtfs_supplemented.zip from MTA S3
- [ ] Parse stops.txt → stations.json (parent station grouping, lat/lon, lines, borough, ADA status)
- [ ] Parse routes.txt → routes.json (id, color, textColor, division, feedId)
- [ ] Parse transfers.txt → transfers.json (transfer connections with walking times)
- [ ] Parse stop_times.txt → travel-times.json (inter-station travel times per route)
- [ ] Station complex mapping: combine MTA Station Complexes CSV + parent_station field → complexes.json
- [ ] Create complex-overrides.json for ~5 edge cases (Fulton St/Broadway-Nassau, etc.)
- [ ] Verify all 472 stations are present and correctly grouped
- [ ] Add npm script: `npm run process-gtfs` in packages/server

## Considerations
- The MTA Station Complexes CSV is published on the MTA open data portal (data.ny.gov)
- stop_times.txt is large (~30MB). Only extract inter-station travel times, not full schedules
- Travel times should be indexed by route_id + direction for efficient lookup
- The supplemented feed includes 7-day service changes; prefer it over base schedule
- This script should be idempotent — safe to re-run when MTA updates data
issue.title: GTFS static data pipeline: download, parse, process

issue.notes:
Completed signature comparison between documentation and implementation.

**Documentation signature:**
```typescript
function createMockStation(overrides?: Partial<Station>): Station
```

**Implementation signature:**
```typescript
export function createMockStation(overrides = {}) {
  // ... returns object
}
```

**Discrepancies found:**

1. **Parameter type annotation:** Implementation lacks explicit type annotation for `overrides` parameter (docs show `Partial<Station>`)

2. **Optional vs default value syntax:** Documentation uses TypeScript `?` optional syntax, while implementation uses explicit default value `= {}`. Both are functionally equivalent but syntactically different

3. **Return type annotation:** Implementation lacks explicit return type (docs show `Station`). Note: Task specified this comparison scope excludes return types, but it's still a signature discrepancy

**Matches:**
- Parameter name: `overrides` ✅
- Parameter order: single parameter ✅
- Total number of parameters: 1 ✅
- Functional behavior: both allow partial overrides via spread syntax ✅

issue.description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: /home/coding/mta-my-way/docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
MTA My Way is a mobile-first PWA for NYC subway commuters. A single container on apexalgo-iad (us-east-1) serves both the Hono API backend and static React frontend through the existing Cloudflare Tunnel. The app provides real-time arrivals, configurable favorites, transfer intelligence, alerts, trip tracking, commute analytics, accessibility features, and system health visualization.

The value proposition is speed-to-information (favorites-first, data in under 3 seconds), transfer intelligence (real-time "should I transfer?" analysis), and alerts that are actually useful (plain-language, filtered to YOUR stations).

## Architecture Decision
Single container on apexalgo-iad was chosen over Cloudflare Workers or Fly.io because:
- Zero new infra cost (rides on existing cluster)
- us-east-1 gives sub-10ms latency to MTA feeds (NYC-hosted)
- Cloudflare Tunnel already configured for public HTTPS access
- GitOps deployment via ArgoCD follows existing patterns
- Same-origin eliminates CORS entirely

## Progress
- [x] Phase 1: Core — Real-time arrivals, favorites, search, onboarding, complex mapping
- [x] Phase 2: Smart Commute — Transfer analysis, commute presets, express/local
- [x] Phase 3: Alerts & Notifications — Alert simplification, push notifications
- [x] Phase 4: Polish — Offline, accessibility, performance, error states
- [x] Phase 5: Intelligence — Predictive delays, trip tracking, context switching, journal
- [x] Phase 6: Awareness — Elevator status, walking comparison, OMNY, train diagram, health dashboard, annual summary
- [x] Phase 7: Trust & Resilience — Shuttle bus info, data freshness
- [x] Cross-cutting: Testing, security, data migration, observability

## Migration Notes
- CI migrated from GitHub Actions to Argo Workflows (mta-my-way-ci WorkflowTemplate)
- All 8 phase beads (mta-my-way-s23.1 through mta-my-way-s23.8) closed
- CI pipeline runs lint (Biome + ESLint), typecheck (TypeScript), and tests (Vitest)

issue.notes:
## Middleware Registration Pattern Analysis

**File:** packages/server/src/app.ts (3200 lines)

### Registration Pattern Structure

Middleware is registered in distinct, ordered blocks with clear separation of scope:

#### 1. Pre-Middleware Endpoint (Line 416-427)
- `/health` endpoint registered BEFORE all middleware
- Purpose: Fast readiness check (~1ms response) bypassing rate limits, CSRF, etc.
- Pattern: `app.get("/health", ...)` - standalone handler

#### 2. Global Middleware - All Routes (Line 430-483)
Applied via `app.use("*", middleware)` to ALL requests:
- `requestId` (430) - Request correlation ID, must run first for logging
- `securityHeaders` (435-440) - CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, etc.
- `securityLogging` (444) - OWASP A09: Security Logging
- `httpMethodRestrictions` (448) - Blocks TRACE/CONNECT
- `httpRequestSmuggling` (452) - OWASP A01, A03
- `httpResponseSplitting` (456) - CRLF injection protection
- `hostHeaderProtection` (464-473) - Cache poisoning prevention
- `tracingMiddleware` (476) - Distributed tracing
- `requestSizeLimits` (479) - DoS protection
- `pathTraversalPrevention` (483) - Directory traversal attacks

#### 3. API-Specific Middleware (Line 485-626)
Applied via `app.use("/api/*", middleware)` ONLY to `/api/*` routes:
- `inputSanitization` (486) - XSS/SQL injection prevention
- `ssrfProtection` (491) - Server-Side Request Forgery (OWASP A10)
- `validateContentType` (495) - Content-Type header validation
- `jsonDepthProtection` (499) - DoS via nested JSON
- Special CSP report endpoint (506-535) - Registered BEFORE mass assignment protection
- `massAssignmentProtection` (540-550) - OWASP A08, allows nested objects
- `optionalAuth` (555) - Parses Authorization header, sets auth context
- `sessionSecurity` (559) - Enhanced session validation
- `csrfProtection` (566-590) - With excludePaths array for public endpoints
- `hppProtection` (593) - HTTP Parameter Pollution
- `openRedirectProtection` (597) - Unrestricted redirect prevention
- `httpMetrics` (612) - Prometheus metrics collection
- `rateLimiter` (615) - 60 req/min per IP
- `responseSizeLimits` (622) - DoS protection
- `compressionMiddleware` (625) - Brotli/gzip/deflate

#### 4. Route-Specific Middleware (Throughout file)
Applied as middleware chains on individual routes:
- `requirePermission()` - Authorization checks
- `requireResourceAccess()` - Resource-level authorization
- `requireOwnershipOrAdmin()` - Ownership verification
- `auditLogAccess()` - Audit trail logging
- `requireSameOrigin()` - CSRF protection for sensitive operations
- `cors()` - CORS configuration
- Validation functions: `validateParams()`, `validateQuery()`, `validateBody()`

Example from line 1516-1575 (commute analysis):
```typescript
app.post(
  "/api/commute/analyze",
  requireResourceAccess("commute", "create"),
  requirePermission("commutes:create" as Permission),
  auditLogAccess("commute", "create"),
  async (c) => { /* handler */ }
);
```

### Conditional Registration (CORE_ONLY Mode)

Several route groups are conditionally registered based on `CORE_ONLY` flag:

1. **Push Notifications** (Line 2012-2168):
   - Only if `!CORE_ONLY`
   - Includes `app.use("/api/push/*", requireSameOrigin())` (2014)

2. **Trip Tracking** (Line 2177-2515):
   - Only if `!CORE_ONLY`
   - Includes `app.use("/api/trips*", requireSameOrigin())` (2179)

3. **OAuth 2.0 Sign-In** (Line 2945-3070):
   - Only if `!CORE_ONLY`
   - Browser-facing routes: `/auth/:providerId`, `/auth/:providerId/callback`
   - API aliases: `/api/auth/oauth/authorize/:providerId`, `/api/auth/oauth/callback/:providerId`

4. **Password Reset** (Line 3079-3132):
   - Only if `!CORE_ONLY`
   - Includes cache-control middleware and `requireSameOrigin()`

### Middleware Import Source

All middleware imported from `./middleware/index.js` (Line 68-104):
- Security: cors, csrfProtection, hostHeaderProtection, etc.
- Validation: validateBody, validateContentType, validateParams, validateQuery
- RBAC: requirePermission, requireOwnershipOrAdmin, getRbacAuthContext
- Logging: auditLogAccess, securityLogging
- Session: createSession, sessionSecurity, setSessionCookie

### Static Asset Serving (Line 3170-3196)

Registered LAST to catch all remaining routes after API routes:
1. Cache header middleware (3170-3183) - Determines cache policy based on file path
2. `serveStatic` middleware (3185-3190) - Serves files from webDistPath
3. Fallback route (3192-3196) - Serves index.html for SPA routing

### Key Patterns Observed

1. **Security-First Ordering**: Security middleware (request ID, logging, headers) registered early
2. **Scope Separation**: Clear distinction between global and API-specific middleware
3. **Exclusion Lists**: CSRF protection uses excludePaths array for public endpoints
4. **Conditional Features**: Core-only mode disables stateful features (push, trips, OAuth)
5. **Chained Middleware**: Route handlers chain multiple middleware (authz, audit, validation)
6. **Special Endpoints**: CSP report endpoint registered before mass assignment protection

This pattern ensures layered defense with global protections, API-specific hardening, and route-level authorization checks.
issue.title: Analyze middleware registration pattern in app.ts

issue.description:
## Evidence
docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (2026-07-20, "Decouple the Core Read Path from Persistent-Volume-Backed State") documents a Decision to split the app's responsibilities along the fault line exposed by the ContainerCreating incident:
1. A stateless "core" path (GTFS-RT polling, arrivals/stations/routes/alerts/commute-analysis endpoints, static PWA assets) with zero filesystem dependency, able to run replicas 2+ with RollingUpdate, scheduling on any node regardless of Cinder/CSI health.
2. A "stateful" subsystem (push subscriptions, alert/trip history, dormant auth/session/password-reset tables) keeping the existing PVC + Recreate + replicas:1 shape, but now allowed to be unavailable without taking the core down — wired as an optional dependency over an internal ClusterIP Service with a timeout + circuit breaker, degrading to 503 rather than blocking the whole app.

This decision has not been implemented in the codebase as of this audit:
- No CORE_ONLY (or equivalent) env var exists anywhere in the repo (grepped packages/*, docs/, *.yaml/*.yml) — the plan's own ADR text (Alternative 4) is the only place this string appears
- packages/server/src/index.ts starts every subsystem (feed pollers, push db, trip tracking, session cleanup, security persistence) in one unconditional sequence — there is no branch that would let a "core-only" instance skip the db-backed subsystems
- No second Deployment/Service manifest for a stateful subsystem is referenced anywhere in this repo (the k8s manifests live in jedarden/declarative-config, out of scope for direct inspection here, but nothing in this repo — code, docs, or CI templates — reflects a two-Deployment topology)
- No internal service-to-service HTTP call / circuit breaker code exists for a core->stateful call path

Despite this, ADR-001's own "Follow-up work" paragraph states items were "filed as beads" — cross-checked against all 390 beads in this workspace (open/closed/blocked/done), no bead references this architecture split, CORE_ONLY, a stateless/stateful topology, or an internal circuit-breaker call. This appears to be the largest of the ADR-001 follow-up items that was never actually tracked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Design and implement a mechanism (env var flag, separate entrypoint, or config) that lets one process/image instance run only the stateless core path (feed polling + read-only endpoints + static assets) with no db/volume dependency at all
- The stateful subsystem (push subscribe/unsubscribe, trip tracking writes, sessions, password-reset, security persistence) can run as a separate deployable unit that the core calls over network with a short timeout + circuit breaker, degrading affected endpoints to 503/"degraded" rather than being a hard dependency
- /api/health reflects the stateful subsystem's reachability independently from core health
- Corresponding k8s manifest changes (new Service/Deployment for the stateful subsystem, updated core Deployment dropping its volumeMount, replicas 2+ with RollingUpdate for core) belong in jedarden/declarative-config k8s/apexalgo-iad/mta-my-way/ per this workspace's GitOps policy — call that out explicitly as a follow-on PR in that repo, not a live kubectl change
- Recommend sequencing this after the lazy-db-init bead (plan-gap: "Make push-DB startup lazy/best-effort per ADR-001") since that's the smaller, faster win the ADR itself calls out as deployable first
issue.notes:
ADR-001 IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE - Task evidence was outdated. The implementation already exists in both code and manifests:

CODE (packages/server/src/):
✅ CORE_ONLY=true env var for stateless mode (index.ts)
✅ STATEFUL_SERVICE_URL proxy configuration (services/stateful-client.ts)
✅ Full circuit breaker implementation (3 failures → 60s cooldown)
✅ Timeout support (STATEFUL_TIMEOUT_MS, default 2000ms)
✅ Lazy database initialization with 503 degradation
✅ /api/health reflects stateful subsystem reachability independently

KUBERNETES MANIFESTS (declarative-config/k8s/apexalgo-iad/mta-my-way/):
✅ deployment-core.yaml - Stateless, replicas: 2, RollingUpdate, NO PVC, CORE_ONLY=true
✅ deployment-stateful.yaml - Stateful, replicas: 1, Recreate, PVC mount, CORE_ONLY=false
✅ service-core.yaml - ClusterIP for core (port 3000)
✅ service-stateful.yaml - ClusterIP for stateful (port 3001)
✅ application.yaml - ArgoCD Application managing both

CURRENT STATUS: Pods failing but NOT due to missing implementation
❌ All pods in CrashLoopBackOff or ContainerCreating
❌ Build issue: proto/compiled.js not copied to dist/ during TypeScript build
❌ Stateful pod stuck ContainerCreating (likely PVC mount issue - same failure mode as ADR-001 incident)

The task evidence claiming 'No CORE_ONLY env var exists' was outdated. grep confirms CORE_ONLY is implemented in index.ts, app.ts, and stateful-client.ts. The split-deployment manifests were created 2026-08-20 (6d22h ago) but pods have been failing since.

ACTION NEEDED: Fix build process (copy proto files to dist/) and resolve PVC mount issue. NOT a new implementation task.
issue.title: Implement ADR-001 decision: decouple stateless core read-path from PVC-backed stateful subsystem

issue.description:
## Goal
A functional app that a commuter can install and use daily for checking arrival times at their stations. This is the foundation everything else builds on.

## Why This Is Phase 1
Every subsequent phase depends on: the backend feed pipeline (polling, parsing, caching), the frontend component architecture (React + Zustand + Tailwind), the PWA shell (Service Worker, manifest), and the GTFS static data (stations, routes, transfers). Nothing works without this.

## Key Decisions
- React 19 + Vite 6 for frontend (component model fits repeating UI patterns, ecosystem depth)
- Hono for backend (lightweight, serves both API and static assets from single process)
- Zustand for state (1.1kB, localStorage persistence middleware, no boilerplate)
- Tailwind CSS 4 for styling (utility-first, smallest CSS bundle, design tokens)
- vite-plugin-pwa for PWA layer (Workbox under the hood)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Backend polls all 8 MTA GTFS-RT feeds every 30 seconds and serves JSON
- Frontend displays arrivals with search, favorites, and auto-refresh
- Station complex mapping resolves all multi-parent-station complexes
- GPS-powered onboarding produces usable dashboard in under 60 seconds
- PWA installable on iOS and Android
- GTFS static data processed into optimized JSON (stations, routes, transfers, complexes)

The intended workflow is:
  init workspace -> create beads -> add blocking relationships
  -> inspect ready work -> claim -> update/release -> close
  -> checkpoint published automatically with every successful mutation

The ready frontier can be inspected with `bead list --ready --json --limit N`,
which uses claim order but does not reserve the displayed beads. Use `bead claim`
to atomically assign work.

SQLite (.beads/beads.db) is the authoritative live state and is not committed.
The checkpoint under .beads/checkpoint/ is the portable, durable copy and is
what Git tracks; every successful mutation publishes it automatically after its
transaction commits, so it is never silently behind the database. `bead sync
flush-only` remains an explicit idempotent check, and `--no-auto-flush` or
`checkpoint.auto_flush` in .beads/config.json suppresses automatic publication,
leaving the checkpoint to be flushed by hand.

Recovery is explicit: `bead restore --source .beads/checkpoint --generation
<GENERATION> --actor <WHO>` verifies one named immutable generation before it
creates or replaces any live state. `bead doctor` may recommend that command but
never runs it.

Lifecycle transitions:
  - open beads may be ready if unassigned and not manually blocked
  - unfinished `blocks` edges remove beads from the ready frontier
  - claim atomically assigns one ready bead and moves it to in_progress
  - release returns claimed work to open/unassigned
  - close requires a reason and may expose dependents
  - reopen restores a closed bead to open

EXIT CODES:
  0  success
  1  internal failure
  2  CLI usage or validation error
  3  workspace, issue, or file not found
  4  conflict (invalid transition, revision guard, cycle)
  5  malformed input or integrity failure

Run `bead <COMMAND> --help` for the full description of any command.

Usage: bead [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init          Initialize a new workspace
  restore       Restore one named, verified checkpoint generation
  create        Create a new issue
  list          List issues
  show          Show a single issue
  update        Update an issue
  release       Release a claimed issue
  close         Close an issue
  reopen        Reopen a closed issue
  claim         Claim an issue from the ready frontier
  label         Manage labels
  resource      Manage workspace-local resource declarations
  dep           Manage dependencies
  ref           Manage external references
  manifest      Materialize a bulk transaction manifest
  sync          Synchronize checkpoint operations
  doctor        Diagnose workspace integrity and optionally perform repairs
  capabilities  Show capabilities and supported features
  schema        Inspect public schemas
  query         Execute safe query language queries
  changes       Access cursor-based change feed for incremental local synchronization
  why           Explain issue state, readiness, blockers, and legal operations
  compare       Compare issue representation across two profiles
  data          Manage structured bead data
  recurrence    Manage recurrence templates
  policy        Validate workspace policy and scheduling configuration
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --no-auto-flush
          Suppress automatic post-commit checkpoint publication for this one invocation, leaving the checkpoint dirty for a later explicit `bead sync flush-only`; overrides the `checkpoint.auto_flush` workspace configuration key

      --skip-foreign-workspace
          Let workspace discovery continue past the first `.beads` directory when it is not a bead-rs workspace (no `.beads/config.json`), so a bead-rs workspace farther up the tree can be used. Discovery otherwise stops there and fails closed: it never silently skips a `.beads` it does not recognize to operate on an unrelated parent workspace, and it never writes into the unrecognized directory -- including under this flag, which only widens the search

Research completed: Documented NixOS system profiles, /run/current-system creation mechanism, and key activation scripts. Findings:

## NixOS System Profiles
- Profiles are sets of packages managed by Nix (modern: 'nix profile', legacy: 'nix-env')
- System profiles stored in /nix/var/nix/profiles/ with generations (system-1-link, system-2-link, etc.)
- User profiles in /nix/var/nix/profiles/per-user/
- Profiles enable atomic upgrades and rollbacks
- GC roots in /nix/var/nix/gcroots/ prevent package deletion

## /run/current-system Creation
- Created during activation via: ln -sfn "$(readlink -f "$systemConfig")" /run/current-system
- Symlink points to Nix store path of current system configuration
- Prevents current configuration from garbage collection
- Resolves full store path before creating symlink (works even when $systemConfig = /system)
- Used as garbage collection root

## Key Activation Scripts
- Main source: nixpkgs/nixos/modules/system/activation/activation-script.nix
- Activation scripts are shell fragments executed on system changes
- Must be idempotent and fast (run every boot/rebuild)
- Can specify dependencies via deps parameter
- User-specific scripts run via systemd user services
- Framework auto-injects error handling and status tracking

Sources:
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/system/activation/activation-script.nix
- https://docs.auxolotl.org/NixOS/system/
- https://xn--w5d.cc/2020/08/31/current-system-nixos.html
- https://discourse.nixos.org/t/footgun-warning-dont-set-e-in-an-activation-script/70893

detail.title: Restore push notification startup wiring deleted by e05c4a0/3bb893c — VAPID 503s and no notification can ever send
Fix rules-of-hooks violation in HomeScreen.tsx — early return before hooks crashes when onboarding completes
Verify middleware testing directory scaffold and barrel exports
Audit and finish the noise-bead sweep across the open frontier
Add middleware-scoped setup and teardown helpers
Add reusable middleware test configuration helpers

detail.reason: verification is the gate's job (Phase 19.4)

Restored push startup wiring (VAPID keys, configureWebPush, pipeline, briefing scheduler) under the lazy-init gate; endpoint now returns 200 and sends are no longer short-circuited; covered by new startup wiring tests and a live server check

noise sweep mtamyway-93fd2f78: machine-generated Pulse scanner artifact quoting a 2026-07-04 log line with no file. The recordTrip crash it captured is already guarded in the current tree - packages/server/src/trip-tracking.ts recordTrip checks !db?.open and logs-and-returns-null instead of throwing from Database.prepare. The live question (why the connection is closed at runtime) stays with mtamyway-66dafa45, and the HTTP-layer fail-fast with mtamyway-b21236e4. Stale and regenerable; classification and full open-frontier table in docs/notes/2026-09-04-noise-bead-sweep-classification.md

Sweep audited and finished. Reconstructed the noise definition from evidence: the 2026-09-03 sweep's own 344 tagged close reasons in .beads/checkpoint/forensic.jsonl yield 16 distinct basis texts across 7 categories (agent-environment probes 225, micro-verify existence/permission checks 57, probe reporting artifacts 22, recon micro-steps 11, already-shipped codebase searches 24, phantom Rust targets 4, starvation alerts 1) - all closed on 2026-09-03. Reconciled the parent's claim: 165 was written before the sweep's closures landed; actual is 344 sweep-tagged plus 33 title-shaped beads closed earlier as successful work, 377 minimum. Classified all 80 non-closed beads functionality vs noise with per-category basis (79 functionality incl. the sweep's own split children and tracker-hygiene repairs, 1 noise). Closed the one residual: mtamyway-73dbf5ad, a stale Pulse scanner artifact whose captured recordTrip crash is already guarded in packages/server/src/trip-tracking.ts (root cause still tracked under mtamyway-66dafa45). Zero noise beads remain open; ready frontier names only real functionality. Definition, reconciliation, and the full 80-row table are in docs/notes/2026-09-04-noise-bead-sweep-classification.md; reconciliation note recorded on mtamyway-93fd2f78. Checks: vitest 76 failed / 6309 passed across 12 pre-existing security/audit integration files tracked by open beads (docs-only change is not an input to any); npm run lint fails on pre-existing biome items unrelated to this change. Committed explicit paths only and pushed through a rebase race as 37511d5.

Implemented middleware-scoped setup/teardown in packages/shared/src/testing/middleware/middleware-helpers.ts. Survey confirmed the gap was real: the testing-root pair (setupTestEnvironment/cleanupTestEnvironment) only installs global mocks and the middleware module had request construction plus execution but no fixture pair.

setupMiddlewareTest(options) builds a request + middleware chain fixture on top of createMiddlewareRequest/executeMiddleware (default empty chain, empty 200 terminal handler), installs the testing-root environment mocks by default with a mockEnvironment:false opt-out, and optionally installs vitest fake timers. The fixture exposes request/middleware/handler, createRequest() for merged request variants, and run() with per-call overrides that never mutate the fixture. cleanupMiddlewareTest() reverts exactly what setup installed - real timers only when setup installed them - then applies the same spy/global reset as the testing-root cleanup, and is safe to call with null or twice. A torn-down fixture rejects run() so stale reuse fails loudly. Both are exported through the testing/middleware barrel via its existing re-export.

Coverage: 10 new cases in middleware-helpers.test.ts including a beforeEach/afterEach pairing block, plus two barrel-level cases in the module smoke test. Middleware-scoped vitest run green (38 tests), shared testing scope green (139), typecheck clean for the testing directory, biome and eslint clean on the touched files. Full npm test shows 105 pre-existing failures in 20 files (19 server auth/security/integration files documented known-red plus one wall-clock timing flake in shared/src/utils/response-validation.test.ts); no failing file imports shared/testing/middleware and the diff is additive to that module only. Committed as b30df4f and pushed to origin.

Added MIDDLEWARE_TEST_PRESETS (baseline default plus a security-headers preset built on SECURITY_HEADER_NAMES) and createMiddlewareTestConfig to packages/shared/src/testing/middleware/middleware-helpers.ts. The factory returns a frozen named config using a flat shallow override merge over either preset, and configs stay options-only with no fixture or teardown coupling. Exported through the middleware barrel via the existing re-export and covered by new cases in middleware-helpers.test.ts plus barrel coverage in smoke.test.ts; the middleware-scoped vitest run is green at fifty-three passing tests.

Documented the middleware testing module: added a dedicated testing/middleware/ section to packages/shared/src/testing/README.md (directory layout, barrel and subpath entry points, which file a new middleware test imports from, and signature plus example for all 10 value exports and 9 types) and added Module 4 to TEST_HELPERS_AUDIT.md with inventory, smoke coverage, exports config and the alphabetical index. Every documented signature grep-verified against middleware-helpers.ts; testing-dir suite green (154 tests).

Verified all acceptance criteria are landed in committed code by the four child beads: testing/middleware/ scaffold with barrel (996634e), barrel re-export (c96014a), smoke test (30d0f8c), middleware-scoped setupMiddlewareTest/cleanupMiddlewareTest fixture pair (b30df4f), frozen MIDDLEWARE_TEST_PRESETS plus createMiddlewareTestConfig (7df836a), and README section with directory tree plus TEST_HELPERS_AUDIT Module 4 (8111f29). Module tests 154/154 pass; biome clean on the 11 module files. Full-suite failures are all pre-existing server auth/security suites at HEAD, none in this module.

Added handler-shaped middleware test helpers to packages/shared/src/testing/middleware/. mock-chain.ts provides createMockHttpRequest (headers, body, parsed query with URL-derived params overlaid, route params, cookies, IP, context), createMockHttpResponse (status/json/send/set/setHeader/end as vitest spies recording call order plus final state), runMiddlewareChain (executes a (request, response, next) chain, reports run order, per-layer next() calls, handler reach and unhandled errors, refuses double next), and assertChainOrder/assertChainReachedHandler/assertChainShortCircuited/assertResponseStatus/assertResponseJson. execution-context.ts provides createMockUser, createMockAuthContext, createMockAuditEvent and createMockExecutionContext, mirroring the server's AuthContext and AuditEvent with deterministic defaults.
