detail.reason: Audit complete; every inventoried file dispositioned. The described conflict no longer exists: the entire wire-up direction was already committed in a3c48ed4 (12:53 UTC, after this bead's 11:25 UTC inventory), so that inventory was stale. Six web files (journalApi.ts/.test.ts, useJournalSync.ts/.test.tsx, journalStore.ts, App.tsx) = landed, tree clean, 60/60 journal tests green, eslint clean. packages/server/src/app.ts = left-for-owner, tree untouched; its 79+/505- delta bundles three concerns, depends on two symbols absent from HEAD, and its /api/trips+/api/journal deletion is unattributable to any bead (de-scope was only ever an alternative to the now-landed wire-up), while the /healthz portion matches mtamyway-3117ec7a. Reverted: none. Zero source files changed by this bead. The one real action was landing the disposition: a3c48ed4 was local-only, so it was integrated with pull --rebase --autostash (89 dirty paths preserved exactly, disjoint from the VERSION-only origin commit) and pushed; origin/main is now 8641cf42 and CI can see the wire-up. Full detail in notes.

Completed the typed client journal surface in packages/web/src/lib/journalApi.ts. Four endpoint groups were already present from the landed wire-up (listServerTrips, createServerTrip, deleteServerTrip, updateServerTripNotes); this bead adds the remaining four verified against app.ts at HEAD: getServerTrip, getJournalStats, getJournalTripsForDates, and getJournalSummary. Payloads use TripRecord and CommuteStats from shared; the stats fields are typed nullable because calculateCommuteStats can return null behind its own readiness guard. JournalApiError carries the status and classifyJournalFailure sorts it into auth, permanent, and retryable. All eight groups have mocked-fetch coverage including the non-2xx path, and the classifier is asserted on 401, 403, 400, 500, and a network TypeError. Verification: journalApi 21, useJournalSync 12, journalStore 39, all passing on the pushed commit 95c0751c; eslint clean on both files; biome clean on both files; typecheck of packages/web reports zero errors in the changed files. Committed and pushed to Forgejo origin.

Deliverable verified as already landed and pushed at 8641cf42 (feat(web): consume the server journal API with an offline-first sync) — this dispatch was stale, so the work below was audited against the live tree rather than re-derived.

journalStore.ts now carries tripIdentityKey, UNMATCHED_SERVER_COMMUTE_ID and mergeServerRecords; useJournalSync (mounted once in App.tsx beside usePreferencesSync) mirrors local writes to the server through journalApi, local-first.

Acceptance audit against HEAD:
- Signed out: useJournalSync guards every effect and the sync body on authenticated, so zero journal requests are issued; the signed-out case is asserted by useJournalSync.test 'makes no journal request while signed out'. The unauthenticated and forbidden statuses classify as 'auth' in classifyJournalFailure, so they never enter the permanent-rejection path and no rejection escapes unhandled.
- Signed-in write: pushLocalTrips uploads unacknowledged records via createServerTrip and registers the returned server id, so the local journal reflects server confirmation without a re-upload.
- Offline/reconciliation: retryable failures leave the record queued (15s timer plus the browser online event); dedupe is by identity key against the persisted server-id registry, so a pulled record blocks its own re-upload. 'does not duplicate a pulled record on a second merge' covers it.
- Pre-existing device-local entries: the store only gained an additive merge action, persist version 3 and its migrations are untouched, and merge keeps local-only records.
- Tests: journalStore.test.ts covers the local-first write and a full mergeServerRecords reconciliation suite; the offline fallback lives in the sync hook (the store has no network code) and is covered there.

Verification: journalStore.test.ts (39), useJournalSync.test.tsx (12) and journalApi.test.ts (21) all pass — 72/72; eslint clean on all six journal files. No code change was made by this run, so there is nothing to commit; the other workers' uncommitted WIP in the shared checkout was left alone.

Consumption proof landed and pushed at 7c4888fc (test(journal): prove the frontend consumes the server journal routes). The mount half of the scope was already satisfied at HEAD — useJournalSync is called exactly once, in the app shell (packages/web/src/App.tsx line 71, from the landed wire-up 8641cf42), and is auth-gated: the sync effects bail while loading or signed out, syncNow re-checks the auth store, and the debounced mirror pass returns early when signed out, so signed-out users pay no journal polling.

The proof half is new: tests/journal-sync-roundtrip.test.ts (root node vitest project) runs the real zustand journal store, the real sync steps (pushLocalTrips / pullServerTrips), the real client (journalApi), and the real server app (createApp over an in-memory SQLite trip database), stubbing only the transport seam — a fetch shim that swaps the browser session cookie for the API-key Authorization header the server's own auth middleware accepts, the same substitution every packages/server integration test makes. Four tests: (1) a write travels store -> client API -> POST /api/trips -> SQLite and reads back through GET /api/trips into the store under the server-assigned id with the server-resolved station names, the identity key intact, the locally observed source preserved, and /api/journal/summary answering from the same database; (2) the mirror is idempotent — a second pass uploads nothing; (3) a local delete reaches the server copy via the server id the pull registered; (4) a mount-contract guard asserting App.tsx calls useJournalSync exactly once. useJournalSync.test.tsx also gains the StrictMode case: the shell renders inside <StrictMode>, both effect invocations reach syncNow in the same tick, and exactly one upload pass runs (the in-flight guard), pinned past the 750 ms debounced pass.

Verification was done against a clean-room git archive of HEAD plus these two files, because the shared checkout's working tree still carries the unattributable app.ts WIP (79+/505-) that deletes the /api/trips and /api/journal routes — already dispositioned left-for-owner by mtamyway-4ee39d7e — so an in-tree run of the proof 404s. In the clean room: 4/4 round-trip tests green, 73/73 journal web tests green, eslint clean under both the HEAD and the WIP (react-hooks) lint configs, biome clean, and a tsc --build --force A/B with vs without these files produced identical error sets, i.e. zero new type errors (the five pre-existing ones at HEAD are in CommuteEditor.test.tsx and useInferredTrips.test.ts, untouched here). CI's test step builds @mta-my-way/shared before vitest, which this test needs to resolve the package, then runs on a clean clone of main, so it exercises the proof against the committed tree.

After this child no server journal code is live-but-unconsumed: the /api/trips and /api/journal surface is consumed by the frontend through the mounted sync, and the round-trip test is the verifiable evidence. The umbrella mtamyway-7e547a37 (which this bead blocks) is closed naming this test as its verifiable deliverable.

Closed via the consume outcome, which this bead's own terms rank first: wire journalStore to the API with an offline-first fallback, verified by a sync test. The de-scope branch never had an owning child and was made moot when the wire-up landed.

Landed in two commits. 8641cf42 (feat(web): consume the server journal API with an offline-first sync) wired the frontend to the server surface: a typed client (packages/web/src/lib/journalApi.ts covering both /api/trips and /api/journal endpoint groups), an offline-first sync hook (useJournalSync) mounted exactly once in the app shell at packages/web/src/App.tsx line 71 and gated on auth state so signed-out users pay no polling cost, and journalStore.mergeServerRecords to reconcile server trips into the local journal by identity key with server copies winning except the locally observed source. 95c0751c completed the typed client surface with the remaining four endpoints. 7c4888fc (test(journal): prove the frontend consumes the server journal routes) is the verifiable deliverable this bead asked for: tests/journal-sync-roundtrip.test.ts drives a journal write from the real zustand store through the real client onto the real Hono app over a real SQLite trip database and reads it back — store -> pushLocalTrips -> journalApi -> POST /api/trips -> SQLite -> GET /api/trips -> mergeServerRecords -> store under the server-assigned id, plus an idempotence check, a delete round trip, a mount-once guard, and a StrictMode no-double-sync test. Only the transport seam is stubbed (browser session cookie swapped for the API-key header the server's own middleware accepts).

Verified green at the carrying commit in a clean-room git archive of main: 4/4 round-trip tests, 73/73 journal web tests, eslint and biome clean, and a tsc --build --force A/B showing zero new type errors. Every piece of the server journal surface is now consumed by the frontend rather than live-but-unconsumed.
